items.text: “Some of you journaled this week. Some of you didn’t. Both are fine.”
One sentence about what showed up — optional, no pressure
“‘Path soil at school’ — just one sentence. Anyone?”
“The work is happening, whether or not we name it tonight.”
Psalm 139 is the psalm of being completely known by God — and the psalmist’s response is not panic. It is wonder
Most of us have parts we hope nobody has noticed. The psalmist invites God to look further
The opposite of being hidden is not being exposed — it is being seen and being safe at the same time. That is what the circle is
Tonight is a small practice of Psalm 139 — parents answer one question, with what they are willing to say

panel.label: PSALM 139:23–24
lines: “Search me, O God, and know my heart! Try me and know my thoughts! And see if there be any grievous way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting!”

items.text: The Lead Companion tells their own story — five minutes, modeling the form
The one question: “tell the story of how you got here — today, as you are. What has shaped you into who you are today?”
Be specific — “I grew up in a house where I learned to read a slammed cabinet door”
Not the hero, not the victim — what happened, and where you see God in it now, looking back
“That is the form. Parents, you’ll do this in your cluster tonight. Teens, this is yours next week. Yours doesn’t have to look like mine.”
One question — how you got here, and what has shaped you. The depth is yours to choose
Listening — do not fix. Do not advise. Do not say “that happened to me too.” Receive, then bless
Nothing leaves your circle. “Not a phrase, not a name, not a story.”
Teens — your own storytelling card goes home tonight; next Wednesday is your night
Two or three families together, your own family stays with you — thirty-five minutes
Tonight’s tellers: the parents — plus any Companion-in-Formation. The Cluster Companion goes first
Story — 5–7 minutes. The teller speaks; nobody interrupts, even the silences
Silence — ten seconds
Blessing round — one or two sentences each, teens included: “What I want to bless about your story is...”
“Inside this cluster, what is said stays in this cluster. Not even back to the main room, and not back up in the car this week.”
“When someone is telling their story... we are looking at them. We are receiving. That’s the practice.”
What happened in your circle stays in your circle
One word — just one — about what tonight was like for you. You can pass
“Heavy.” “Seen.” “Surprising.” “Tender.” “Hard.” Whatever the true word is
“Each of you brought something true into this room tonight, and each of you received something true. That’s rare. It’s also the kind of room God shows up in.”
Joint Footprints — each parent-and-teen pair sits together once this week. Twenty minutes total
Not in the car, not at dinner, not while the TV is on. Phones away
Five minutes telling the footprints question — where you grew up, who shaped you, what places and people made you who you are
The listener asks one or two follow-ups, then one sentence: “What I love about your footprints is...”
Then swap — the other person tells, the first listens and blesses
The morning question and evening journal note continue daily
